pool.text: Emperor Charles V granted the coat of arms to the New Kingdom of Granada.
The city became the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Bogotá.
The National Library of Colombia was established as a dependence of the Ministry of Culture.
An insurgency movement began against the colonial authorities with rebel armbands.
The Public Library, now the National Library, was enlarged and modernized.
The statue of Bolivar was unveiled on the Independence Day of Colombia.
The coat of arms was officially recognized and adopted as the symbol of Bogotá.
Liberal leader Jorge Eliecer Gaitan was assassinated, resulting in destructive downtown riots.
Decree 555 officially adopted the patriotic armband as the flag of Bogotá.
Construction of the airport was ordered by Gustavo Rojas Pinilla to replace Techo Airport.
The Biblioteca Luis Angel Arango was established as a dependence of the Bank of the Republic.
Bogotá became part of the Union of Ibero-American Capital Cities.
A participatory and integrated security policy named Comunidad Segura was first adopted.
The TransMilenio system of articulated buses opened its first phase in the city.
The orchid Odontoglossum luteopurpureum was adopted as the emblematic flower of Bogotá.
The explosion of a car bomb in a parking lot at El Nogal Club left casualties.
Futsal was established as the symbolic sport of the city by City Council Agreement.
Bus routes for Suba Avenue and Southern Highway were opened.
UNESCO named Bogotá as the World Book Capital.
A car bomb was detonated in front of a complex of buildings housing Caracol Radio.
